clue.text: A fellow unable to walk has got fired

parts.note: lame describes someone who cannot walk properly

explanation.surface: A disabled colleague has been dismissed from his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' reads as sacked, but here it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burning is on fire, ablaze, so it has been fired in the sense of ignited.

clue.text: Just limiting learners ability

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in, so the word for just surrounds the learner letter

parts.note: just, as in even-handed, means fair
L is the learner plate letter

explanation.surface: Merely restricting students' talent.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural talent or knack is a flair for something, so both name ability.

clue.text: Perhaps kind of orders for desserts?

definitions.text: Perhaps kind of orders for desserts?

parts.words: Perhaps kind of orders for desserts?
parts.note: reads as a restaurant's dessert orders, but refers to the phrase for perfect neatness, which names a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A waiter wonders what sort of pudding orders are coming in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple-pie order' is an idiom for perfect tidiness, so these desserts are a kind of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit-filled pastry puddings are desserts, and their name also describes immaculate order.

clue.text: Less than often ought to be sufficient

indicators.note: says the answer is less than the whole of the words, a run taken from inside them

explanation.surface: Doing less than one often should is still adequate.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is hidden across 'oftEN OUGHt'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty or adequate: both words describe having as much as is needed.

clue.text: Where cattle are quick going in and late coming out?

definitions.text: Where cattle are quick going in and late coming out?

parts.words: Where cattle are quick going in and late coming out?
parts.note: quick is the old word for alive and late means dead, so the animals enter living and leave slaughtered

explanation.surface: A farm where livestock move fast on the way in but dawdle leaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' and 'late' look like speeds and times; they are the old senses alive and deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: A slaughterhouse is the building where livestock are killed for meat.

clue.text: State in exposure needs temperature and humidity control

indicators.note: one word placed inside the other, so the state goes inside the exposure

parts.note: an airing is exposure to the open air
state, as in shape or health, means condition

explanation.surface: A national exposé demands climate regulation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cooling and dehumidifying systems regulate indoor climate, controlling heat and moisture.

clue.text: Suspension of a governor misusing cane

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: misusing the letters of cane means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A colonial governor is caning people improperly and is suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: When a matter is in abeyance it is temporarily halted, held in suspension.

clue.text: Sort of owl succeeded in losing nothing in river

indicators.note: the second in places the shortened word inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the word for succeeded

parts.note: succeeded, as in triumphed, means won
O is the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: An owl that managed to lose nothing while in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is a link; 'losing' drops the nothing letter from the win word, and the Tay is the longest river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The tawny is a common brown woodland species of owl.

clue.text: Sincere flattery?

parts.note: points to the proverb that copying someone is the sincerest form of flattery

explanation.surface: A compliment that is genuinely meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying, by the proverb, is the sincerest way of paying a compliment.

clue.text: Building regulations require this rather wet set of instructions

parts.note: damp means slightly wet
a course is a series of lessons

explanation.surface: Planning rules demand some soggy training.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a waterproof layer laid in a wall near the ground, which building rules make compulsory.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof layer in brickwork stopping rising moisture is mandated by construction rules.

clue.text: Advanced in intelligence given a delay

indicators.note: the advanced letter goes inside the word for intelligence

parts.note: wit means mental sharpness
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level

explanation.surface: Being clever gets you held up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang on or hold back is to postpone, so a pause or postponement is a delay.

clue.text: A number of notes for Margaret in cashing a giro

indicators.note: the short name is put inside the rearranged letters
cashing a cheque turns it into something else, so the letters of a giro are changed

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret is counting banknotes while paying in a giro cheque.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashing' rearranges A GIRO around the pet name. A giro is a British state benefit cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: A broken chord plays its several pitches one after another, so it is a run of musical tones.

clue.text: Whatever happens certainly includes New York & Washington

indicators.note: the word for certainly takes the two abbreviations into its middle

parts.note: ay is a form of aye, yes
WA is the postal abbreviation for Washington State

explanation.surface: However things turn out, it definitely covers both big American cities.
explanation.definitionFit: In any case, regardless of events: both mean no matter what.

clue.text: Some thug lifted fruit

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A thug has stolen some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine.

clue.text: Meter in plant indicates semiconductor

indicators.note: the letter for meter is set inside the flower's name

parts.note: the geranium is a garden plant
M is the symbol for metre

explanation.surface: A gauge inside a factory points to a chip component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This chemical element, atomic number 32, was used in early transistors as a semiconducting material.

clue.text: Old PR deceit is pathetic

indicators.note: something pathetic is in a sorry state, so the letters are mangled

explanation.surface: Ancient public relations trickery is lame.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn out and infirm through age, so very old.

clue.text: Basic thing found in table, aluminium

parts.note: each entry in the periodic table is an element
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Something fundamental sits in the chart next to aluminium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' suggests furniture; it is the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundamental or primary, as in elemental forces, means basic.

clue.text: Tease European twice, nastily, getting complaint

indicators.note: the rearranged group is written two times over
nastily suggests rough treatment, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them

explanation.surface: Teasing a European twice, unkindly, leads to a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nastily' turns RIB + E into BERI, and 'twice' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical disease from vitamin deficiency is an illness, a medical complaint.

clue.text: Outlook for half the viewers

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: only half the word for viewers is kept, its second five letters dropped

parts.note: spectators are people watching

explanation.surface: A view shared by half the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half the' keeps SPECT, the first half of SPECTATORS.
explanation.definitionFit: A view ahead, or expectation for the future, is an outlook.

clue.text: Bird never flies without displaying velocity

indicators.note: flies suggests letters scattering about, so they are rearranged
the velocity letter is not displayed, so it is taken away

parts.note: v is the physics symbol for velocity

explanation.surface: A bird that never takes off without showing its speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without displaying' removes V from NEVER, leaving NEER, which 'flies' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The white-tailed eagle, a sea eagle, is a crossword's favourite bird.

clue.text: Nurse keeps much back that's dishonestly acquired

indicators.note: the nurse holds the turned word inside

parts.note: SEN is a State Enrolled Nurse

indicators.note: the word for much is written back to front

parts.note: a lot means much

explanation.surface: A nurse hoards plenty that was obtained by crooked means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for much. SEN was the old British grade of State Enrolled Nurse.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken by theft, so obtained illegally.

clue.text: On reflection I dispose of a weak animal

indicators.note: a mirror reflection reverses, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to tip rubbish is to get rid of it

explanation.surface: After thinking it over, I put down a feeble creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' reverses I TIP A W as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American elk is a large deer, a wild animal.

clue.text: One's getting good facilities in a place to live

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the loo is a lavatory, euphemistically the facilities

explanation.surface: A home is decent if it has good bathroom amenities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facilities' is the British euphemism for a toilet, LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome-shaped snow house built by Inuit is a dwelling.

clue.text: Possibly appearing in a court he'll get community service?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A defendant in court may be sentenced to unpaid work.
explanation.walkthrough: Only HE of 'he'll' is fodder; the surface plays on community service as a court sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Welfare work reaching out to people in a neighbourhood is a public service.

clue.text: Tea's drunk in Eastern country

indicators.note: a drink taken in is swallowed, so the tea takes the little word inside

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea

explanation.surface: Tea is drunk in an Asian land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' reads as anagram; here the tea, CHA, has drunk IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The People's Republic in East Asia is a nation of the Orient.

clue.text: Power's given to hostile disagreeable person

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
ill, as in ill will, means hostile

explanation.surface: Authority handed to an unfriendly, unpleasant man.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome, unpleasant individual is a bore, an old slang sense.

clue.text: Swine with much in place returned a bit throaty

indicators.note: the animal and the quantity go inside the turned word
the word for place is written back to front

parts.note: a site is a place
a pig is a swine
a lot means much

explanation.surface: A pig with plenty at home came back croaky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses the place word, and the animal and quantity sit inside it after its first letter; 'a bit throaty' means a part of the throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap of cartilage at the throat's entrance is a small part of the throat.

clue.text: One male, modelling, is dignified

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a model sitting for an artist is posing

explanation.surface: A single man working as a model is stately.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand and impressive in bearing, so stately.

clue.text: Foreign ailing animal

indicators.note: foreign suggests something strange and altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sick creature from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian blue bull is a large antelope.
